entities.name: Paclitaxel
observations: Paclitaxel was tested with dichloromethane Urtica dioica extract in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells; co-treatment reportedly decreased paclitaxel IC50 and increased cellular sensitivity.
Formal synergy was not established in the accessible report because combination-index or equivalent dose-matrix analysis was not reported.

entities.name: Urtica dioica extract
observations: Dichloromethane Urtica dioica extract was combined with paclitaxel in MDA-MB-468 cells and reported to enhance paclitaxel sensitivity.
The extract also showed independent growth-inhibitory and pro-apoptotic activity in MDA-MB-468 cells in a separate study without paclitaxel.

entities.name: MDA-MB-468
observations: Human breast cancer cell line used in the direct Urtica dioica extract plus paclitaxel study; co-treatment reportedly reduced paclitaxel IC50 and increased sensitivity.

entities.name: PMID:27501501
observations: Mohammadi et al. (2016) directly tested dichloromethane Urtica dioica extract plus paclitaxel in MDA-MB-468 cells using MTT, cell-cycle, and migration assays; the report described decreased paclitaxel IC50, increased sensitivity, G2/M arrest, and reduced migration.
Accessible evidence did not establish formal pharmacologic synergy quantitatively.

entities.name: Urtica-paclitaxel sensitization
observations: In MDA-MB-468 cells, dichloromethane Urtica dioica extract plus paclitaxel reportedly decreased the paclitaxel IC50 and substantially increased cellular sensitivity versus treatment context described in the primary study.
This supports sensitization/enhanced response, but not a definitive claim of formal synergy.
